./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14454:Line 110 is exactly the `throw` on the failure branch of `Uri.TryCreate`. So `Uri.TryCreate("https://potato@example.com/9", Absolute, …)` is returning **false** on the Fedora .NET 10 runtime, *and* my `StripLegacySecretKey` is returning the input unchanged (no `@`, no colon-in-userinfo, so it short-circuits). Result: parser dies.
./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14456:**Why does `Uri.TryCreate` reject `https://potato@example.com/9`?** Because the bracket `[` in `[email]` triggers `Uri`'s IPv6 address parser. `https://[...]` is the syntax for `https://[2001:db8::1]/...`. The contents of the brackets must look like a valid IPv6 address, and `email protected` doesn't, so `Uri.TryCreate` rejects the whole string.
./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14461:2. **Recognise this for what it is: an upstream data corruption issue.** The dump export script (or whatever processed the original test file) replaced an email-like substring with the Cloudflare email-obfuscation placeholder `potato@example.com`. This same corruption is now in the actual test source on disk. The test was originally meant to verify legacy `pubkey:potato@example.com` parsing. After corruption it's now a different test that parses an invalid URL.

./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14621:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:10595:Now let me also look at an issue I forgot: my test `AddInfrastructure_TelemetryOnWithValidDsn_ProviderStillBuilds` has a DSN `https://potato@example.com/2`. The OTLP exporter will try to flush spans/logs on shutdown. **Network calls happen on dispose** — and `Dispose` runs via the service provider GC. ./docs/llm/vendor/output/045.txt:51:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14456:**Why does `Uri.TryCreate` reject `https://potato@example.com/9`?** Because the bracket `[` in `[email]` triggers `Uri`'s IPv6 address parser. `https://[...]` is the syntax for `https://[2001:db8::1]/...`. The contents of the brackets must look like a valid IPv6 address, and `email protected` doesn't, so `Uri.TryCreate` rejects the whole string.
./docs/llm/vendor/output/045.txt:52:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14461:2. **Recognise this for what it is: an upstream data corruption issue.** The dump export script (or whatever processed the original test file) replaced an email-like substring with the Cloudflare email-obfuscation placeholder `potato@example.com`. This same corruption is now in the actual test source on disk. The test was originally meant to verify legacy `pubkey:potato@example.com` parsing. After corruption it's now a different test that parses an invalid URL.

./docs/llm/vendor/output/045.txt:127:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14621:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:10595:Now let me also look at an issue I forgot: my test `AddInfrastructure_TelemetryOnWithValidDsn_ProviderStillBuilds` has a DSN `https://potato@example.com/2`. The OTLP exporter will try to flush spans/logs on shutdown. **Network calls happen on dispose** — and `Dispose` runs via the service provider GC. In my test, I don't dispose the provider explicitly, so it lives until the test class is collected. But xUnit calls `IDisposable.Dispose` on my test class, and the service provider is local to the test method (not stored on `this`), so it's also subject to GC.

./docs/llm/vendor/output/045.txt:167:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14667:Good — that grep confirms it. The `potato@example.com` corruption is widespread throughout the test file, not just in the one failing test. The other tests happen to pass because their assertions are *string-equality* — they store `"https://potato@example.com/1"` in config, then assert `options.Sentry.Dsn.ShouldBe("https://potato@example.com/1")`. Since both sides have the same corrupted string, equality holds. The legacy-format test fails because it actually feeds the DSN through `Parse`, which does URL surgery and trips over the brackets.

./docs/llm/vendor/output/045.txt:217:./docs/llm/vendor/output/044.txt:393:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:10595:Now let me also look at an issue I forgot: my test `AddInfrastructure_TelemetryOnWithValidDsn_ProviderStillBuilds` has a DSN `https://potato@example.com/2`. The OTLP exporter will try to flush spans/logs on shutdown. **Network calls happen on dispose** — and `Dispose` runs via the service provider GC. In my test, I don't dispose the provider explicitly, so it lives until the test class is collected. But xUnit calls `IDisposable.Dispose` on my test class, and the service provider is local to the test method (not stored on `this`), so it's also subject to GC.

./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14454:Line 110 is exactly the `throw` on the failure branch of `Uri.TryCreate`. Result: parser dies.
./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14456:**Why does `Uri.TryCreate` reject `https://potato@example.com/9`?** Because the bracket `[` in `[email]` triggers `Uri`'s IPv6 address parser. `https://[...]` is the syntax for `https://[2001:db8::1]/...`. The contents of the brackets must look like a valid IPv6 address, and `email protected` doesn't, so `Uri.TryCreate` rejects the whole string.
./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14461:2. **Recognise this for what it is: an upstream data corruption issue.** The dump export script (or whatever processed the original test file) replaced an email-like substring with the Cloudflare email-obfuscation placeholder `potato@example.com`. This same corruption is now in the actual test source on disk. The test was originally meant to verify legacy `pubkey:potato@example.com` parsing. After corruption it's now a different test that parses an invalid URL.

./docs/llm/vendor/output/045.txt:51:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14456:**Why does `Uri.TryCreate` reject `https://potato@example.com/9`?** Because the bracket `[` in `[email]` triggers `Uri`'s IPv6 address parser. `https://[...]` is the syntax for `https://[2001:db8::1]/...`. The contents of the brackets must look like a valid IPv6 address, and `email protected` doesn't, so `Uri.TryCreate` rejects the whole string.
./docs/llm/vendor/output/045.txt:52:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14461:2. **Recognise this for what it is: an upstream data corruption issue.** The dump export script (or whatever processed the original test file) replaced an email-like substring with the Cloudflare email-obfuscation placeholder `potato@example.com`. This same corruption is now in the actual test source on disk. The test was originally meant to verify legacy `pubkey:potato@example.com` parsing. After corruption it's now a different test that parses an invalid URL.

./docs/llm/vendor/output/045.txt:127:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:14621:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:10595:Now let me also look at an issue I forgot: my test `AddInfrastructure_TelemetryOnWithValidDsn_ProviderStillBuilds` has a DSN `https://potato@example.com/2`. The OTLP exporter will try to flush spans/logs on shutdown. **Network calls happen on dispose** — and `Dispose` runs via the service provider GC. In my test, I don't dispose the provider explicitly, so it lives until the test class is collected. But xUnit calls `IDisposable.Dispose` on my test class, and the service provider is local to the test method (not stored on `this`), so it's also subject to GC.

./docs/llm/vendor/output/045.txt:217:./docs/llm/vendor/output/044.txt:393:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:10595:Now let me also look at an issue I forgot: my test `AddInfrastructure_TelemetryOnWithValidDsn_ProviderStillBuilds` has a DSN `https://potato@example.com/2`. The OTLP exporter will try to flush spans/logs on shutdown. **Network calls happen on dispose** — and `Dispose` runs via the service provider GC. In my test, I don't dispose the provider explicitly, so it lives until the test class is collected. But xUnit calls `IDisposable.Dispose` on my test class, and the service provider is local to the test method (not stored on `this`), so it's also subject to GC.
./docs/llm/vendor/output/045.txt:218:./docs/llm/vendor/output/044.txt:394:./docs/llm/vendor/claude.md:10603:Wait, I should also check whether my DSN parser is too strict. Looking at `[InlineData("https://potato@example.com")]` (no project id) — `Uri.AbsolutePath` of `https://potato@example.com` is `/`. So `Trim('/')` produces `""`. Split by `'/'` produces `[""]`. First element is `""`. So `IsNullOrWhiteSpace("")` is true. Error returned. ✅
